import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Symptom

You raise `PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER` (the request-worker count, see the `50-cluster.conf`
systemd drop-in) to a high number and `:3070` flaps — `READY 32 listeners` for a
moment, then listeners collapse (32 → 11 → 0). The journal is full of:

```
[hono-host] fatal uncaughtException — exiting: Error: ENOSPC: System limit for
number of file watchers reached, watch '…/.papercusp/session-claude/…/.claude.json.lock'
[harness-fs-watcher] enabled-plugins chokidar error: ENOSPC: System limit … reached
```

Each fatal exit → systemd respawn → respawn re-hits ENOSPC → **crash loop**, full
outage of the green operator.

## Root cause

`node:cluster` runs the SAME `runBootstrap()` in every process — the primary **and**
every request worker. Two of the things it starts are recursive `chokidar` / `fs.watch`
file watchers:

- **`ensureHarnessFsWatcher()`** — watches every registered project's `.papercusp/`
  tree to mirror it into PG. On a box with many harnesses this is **~62,000 inotify
  watches per process** (measured).
- **`startClaudeCredentialSync()`** — a `recursive: true` watch on the session-claude
  root.

So `N` workers hold `N × 62k` watches. At 15 workers the box sat at ~1.2M watches; at
32 workers it projects to ~2.2M, which crossed the (then) `fs.inotify.max_user_watches`
= 2,097,152 ceiling. inotify `inotify_add_watch` then returns `ENOSPC`, and the
credential-sync watcher's error was **uncaught** → the hono-host fatal guard exited.

<Aside type="caution">
The kernel limit being hit is `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` (a per-**user** total
across all processes), NOT a per-process ulimit and NOT `max_user_instances`. Because
it is per-user, the dev box's *whole fleet* (agents, harnesses, federation lanes,
VS Code) shares the budget — the cluster just tips an already-busy box over.
</Aside>

## Fixes

Three layers, in order of correctness:

**Current behavior (2026-06-25):** `apps/operator/bin/host-bootstrap.ts` now
starts both `ensureHarnessFsWatcher()` and `startClaudeCredentialSync()` only
when `cluster.isPrimary` is true. `apps/operator/bin/host-benign-errors.ts`
also classifies inotify watcher `ENOSPC` as benign via `isBenignFileWatcherError`,
while leaving disk-full `ENOSPC` fatal.

1. **Run the watchers on ONE process — gate on `cluster.isPrimary`** (the real fix).
   In `host-bootstrap.ts` both watchers are wrapped in `if (cluster.isPrimary) { … }`.
   `cluster.isPrimary` is `true` on the cluster primary **and** on a non-clustered
   single-process host (`:3170`, desktop), `false` only on a forked request worker — so
   the watcher keeps working everywhere it did before, but stops multiplying across
   cluster workers (33 procs × 62k → 1 × 62k). Safe because request workers read the
   mirrored rows via `@papercusp/sync` / the converged on-disk creds; they never needed
   their own watcher.

2. **Make watcher-ENOSPC a benign host error** (robustness). `host-benign-errors.ts`
   `isBenignFileWatcherError()` classifies inotify watch-ENOSPC as log-and-keep-serving
   instead of fatal. Scoped to `syscall === 'watch'` / the "number of file watchers"
   message so a genuine **disk-full** ENOSPC (`syscall` write/open, "no space left on
   device") still fails fast. A missing file watcher must only degrade a background
   convenience, never down the multi-tenant host.

3. **Raise the kernel ceiling** (interim capacity, `/etc/sysctl.conf`
   `fs.inotify.max_user_watches`, persistent). On 2026-06-24 it was raised
   2,097,152 → 4,194,304 to let 32 workers run before fix #1 deployed. Once #1 ships
   the cluster needs only ~62k watches and this raise is no longer load-bearing (but a
   big fleet box benefits from the headroom regardless).

<Aside type="danger">
**Do NOT gate these watchers on `backgroundWorkersEnabled()`.** The dev-api drop-in
sets `PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0` **service-wide**, which the cluster *primary*
inherits too (only workers additionally get it via the cluster `workerEnv`). So
`backgroundWorkersEnabled()` is `false` on the primary as well — gating on it would
disable the FS→PG mirror on **every** process and silently stale the harness panels.
`cluster.isPrimary` is the correct signal. (Alternatively: stop setting
`BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0` service-wide and let the cluster set it on workers only.)
</Aside>

## Scaling the cluster safely

- Bump `PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER` in `~/.config/systemd/user/papercup-dev-api.service.d/50-cluster.conf`,
  `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, then restart via the `dev-server` resource lock.
- After restart, **verify it holds** — sample `ss -ltnp | grep :3070 | grep -oE 'pid=[0-9]+' | sort -u | wc -l`
  several times over ~45s (a one-shot check misses a crash loop), and
  `journalctl --user -u papercup-dev-api.service | grep -c ENOSPC` (must be 0).
- Watch budget: `cat /proc/*/fdinfo/* | grep -c '^inotify'` is total watches in use;
  compare to `/proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_watches`. Per-worker cost ≈ the harness
  count, so it grows as harnesses accumulate.
- Connections are NOT the limit (PgBouncer bounds PG backends independent of worker
  count — see [pg-connection-exhaustion](/internal/docs/agent-insights/pg-connection-exhaustion-too-many-clients)).
  The file-watcher budget is.

Tracked as EI-3385.

## Boot-failure backstop (`onUnbootable`, 2026-06-25)

A separate enhancement in `cluster-fork.ts` (same file): an optional
`onUnbootable` callback arms a **fast-stop** when workers cannot boot at all —
distinct from a runtime crash that happens after a worker is healthy.

The heuristic: a worker that exits within `bootGraceMs` (default **10 s**) of
being forked is counted as a **consecutive boot failure**. Once
`consecutiveBootFailures >= workers` (every slot in the cluster has failed to
boot, with no worker ever staying up past the grace threshold), the cluster
declares itself **UNBOOTABLE**, logs a fatal, and calls `onUnbootable` instead
of respawning into an infinite crash loop.

Key state tracked per cluster lifecycle:
- `sawHealthy` — true once ANY worker has survived past `bootGraceMs`; if set,
  a fast exit is treated as a normal runtime crash and respawned within budget
  (the build can boot, this is a runtime failure).
- `consecutiveBootFailures` — count of workers that exited inside the grace
  window before any worker was seen healthy; reset to 0 when `sawHealthy` flips.

This backstop is **OPT-IN** — pass `onUnbootable` to arm it; without it the
legacy respawn-budget behaviour continues. The production runner passes it so
that a build that can never start (wrong Node version, missing native dep,
MODULE_NOT_FOUND at startup) stops fast and surfaces cleanly instead of
thrashing systemd's restart throttle.
